title: Changes in and about a stream · authority
finding: Changes in and about a stream may only be made in accordance with a change approval, the regulations, an authorization or an order. On these answers a change the block makes rests on none of them.

actions.description: List each crossing with the authority it is made under: the forest route of WSR §39(2), a change §39(1) lists, or a change approval applied for under §11(1) before the work.

title: Change approval, authorization or order · terms
finding: A change approval is issued on application, and a change under it, under an authorization or under an order may only be made in accordance with its terms and conditions. On these answers one relied on is not yet issued, or the work departs from it.

actions.description: Apply for the change approval (§§11(1), 12) before the work, and plan the crossing within its terms and conditions.

title: Forest road crossings under FRPA
finding: WSR §39(2) makes a change to which a FRPA standard applies an authorized change only when a person it names makes it and complies with FRPA and its regulations and standards. On these answers a change relied on under §39(2) is not authorized by it.

actions.description: Bring the crossing within FRPA and FPPR (§§55–57 on stream crossings, fish passage and fish habitat among them), or authorize it another way: a change §39(1) lists, with its notice, or a change approval.

title: An engineer requires a change approval
finding: An engineer who considers that an authorized change may significantly affect the stream, its flow or its channel may require an application for a change approval or authorization, and the change may then not be carried out under Part 3.

actions.description: Apply for the change approval or authorization the engineer requires before the work.

title: A habitat officer’s terms
finding: A change under Part 3 must be made in accordance with the terms and conditions a habitat officer specified under §44, the timing window among them. On these answers the work is not planned within them.

actions.description: Schedule and plan the crossing work within the habitat officer’s terms, or ask the officer about them.

title: Notice to a habitat officer, 45 days ahead
finding: A person proposing a change §39(1) lists must give a habitat officer signed notice of its particulars, on the comptroller’s form, at least 45 days before beginning it.

actions.description: Give the notice at least 45 days before the crossing work, and record when the officer received it.

exceptions.label: Every change under §39(1) is one §38(1) leaves out: emergency flood works or clearing an obstruction from a bridge or culvert by government during a flood (§39(1)(o)–(p)), installing or cleaning drainage outlets (q), repairing a bridge’s superstructure (r) or a fence (s)
evidence: Each change and the paragraph of §39(1) it is made under

title: The habitat officer’s statement of terms
finding: After notice, the person must obtain a habitat officer’s statement of the §44(2) terms and conditions on which the change can proceed.

actions.description: Obtain the statement before the work, and plan the crossing within its terms.

exceptions.label: A habitat officer did not contact the person within 45 days after receiving the notice (§38(4))
evidence: The notice and the date the officer received it

exceptions.label: Every change under §39(1) is one §38(1) leaves out: emergency flood works or clearing an obstruction from a bridge or culvert by government during a flood (§39(1)(o)–(p)), installing or cleaning drainage outlets (q), repairing a bridge’s superstructure (r) or a fence (s)
evidence: Each change and the paragraph of §39(1) it is made under

title: Culvert · 600 mm minimum
finding: A culvert under §39(1)(a) needs an equivalent diameter of at least 600 mm. On these answers it does not, so the change is not an authorized change under Part 3 and needs a change approval or another authority (Water Sustainability Act §11(2)), unless §39(2) covers it.

actions.description: Redesign the culvert to meet the condition, or apply for a change approval before the work, and record each crossing with its station, stream and design.

title: Culvert · 300 mm cover
finding: A culvert under §39(1)(a) needs at least 300 mm of fill cover, or the cover its manufacturer’s specifications require. On these answers it does not, so the change is not an authorized change under Part 3 and needs a change approval or another authority (Water Sustainability Act §11(2)), unless §39(2) covers it.

actions.description: Redesign the culvert to meet the condition, or apply for a change approval before the work, and record each crossing with its station, stream and design.

exceptions.label: The culvert manufacturer’s specifications require a different depth of cover, and the culvert has it (§39(1)(a)(xiii))
evidence: The manufacturer’s specification for the culvert

title: Culvert · 2 m of fill at most
finding: A culvert under §39(1)(a) may have no more than 2 m of fill above its top. On these answers it does not, so the change is not an authorized change under Part 3 and needs a change approval or another authority (Water Sustainability Act §11(2)), unless §39(2) covers it.

actions.description: Redesign the culvert to meet the condition, or apply for a change approval before the work, and record each crossing with its station, stream and design.

title: Culvert · capacity
finding: A culvert under §39(1)(a) needs the stream channel’s hydraulic capacity, or must pass the 1 in 200 year maximum daily flow without the water at its inlet rising above its top. On these answers it does not, so the change is not an authorized change under Part 3 and needs a change approval or another authority (Water Sustainability Act §11(2)), unless §39(2) covers it.

actions.description: Redesign the culvert to meet the condition, or apply for a change approval before the work, and record each crossing with its station, stream and design.

title: Culvert · fish passage
finding: On a fish-bearing stream, a culvert under §39(1)(a) must let fish pass up and down stream under all flow conditions. On these answers it does not, so the change is not an authorized change under Part 3 and needs a change approval or another authority (Water Sustainability Act §11(2)), unless §39(2) covers it.

actions.description: Redesign the crossing, as a clear span bridge or an embedded culvert, to meet the condition, or apply for a change approval before the work, and record each crossing with its station, stream and design.

title: Culvert · engineered design
finding: A culvert of 2 m or greater equivalent diameter, or designed for more than 6 m³ a second, must be designed by an engineering professional and built to that design. On these answers it does not, so the change is not an authorized change under Part 3 and needs a change approval or another authority (Water Sustainability Act §11(2)), unless §39(2) covers it.

actions.description: Have an engineering professional design the culvert and build it to that design, or apply for a change approval before the work.

title: Culvert · installation
finding: A culvert under §39(1)(a) must also be installed from a dry channel or the top of the bank, protected against erosion at both ends, pass debris, leave the channel stable, raise no backwater, allow obstacles to be cleared, leave the channel outside the right of way unaltered, keep fill off its ends and be of CSA materials. On these answers it does not, so the change is not an authorized change under Part 3 and needs a change approval or another authority (Water Sustainability Act §11(2)), unless §39(2) covers it.

actions.description: Redesign the culvert or its installation to meet the condition, or apply for a change approval before the work, and record each crossing with its station, stream and design.

title: Clear span bridge
finding: A clear span bridge is an authorized change under §39(1)(b) only while every condition of that paragraph holds. On these answers it does not, so the change is not an authorized change under Part 3 and needs a change approval or another authority (Water Sustainability Act §11(2)), unless §39(2) covers it.

actions.description: Redesign the bridge to meet the condition, or apply for a change approval before the work, and record each crossing with its station, stream and design.

title: Temporary ford
finding: A temporary ford is an authorized change under §39(1)(v) only while every condition of that paragraph holds. On these answers it does not, so the change is not an authorized change under Part 3 and needs a change approval or another authority (Water Sustainability Act §11(2)), unless §39(2) covers it.

actions.description: Redesign the ford, its timing or its removal to meet the condition, or apply for a change approval before the work, and record each crossing with its station, stream and design.

title: Ice bridge, winter ford or snowfill
finding: An ice bridge, winter ford or snowfill is an authorized change under §39(1)(n) only while every condition of that paragraph holds. On these answers it does not, so the change is not an authorized change under Part 3 and needs a change approval or another authority (Water Sustainability Act §11(2)), unless §39(2) covers it.

actions.description: Redesign the winter crossing and plan its removal before breakup to meet the condition, or apply for a change approval before the work, and record each crossing with its station, stream and design.

title: Damage to the aquatic ecosystem
finding: A person making a change under Part 3, the §39(2) forest route included, who damages the aquatic ecosystem must report it to a habitat officer within 72 hours, and repair the damage and restore the ecosystem as it was or as the officer directs.

actions.description: Inspect the crossings during and after the work; report any damage to the aquatic ecosystem to a habitat officer within 72 hours, and record the repair.
